sentences.text: Kaijutitan is a genus of basal titanosaur dinosaur named after Japanese movie monsters, described by Filippi, Salgado, and Garrido in 2019. The only known species is Kaijutitan maui, and it belongs to the unranked family Titanosauria.
The species is known from a partial skeleton holotype stored at the Museo Municipal Argentino Urquiza.
Its anterior cervical vertebrae possess bifid neural spines and feature a posterior keel created by the backward convergence of a shelf from each parapophysis and the lower rib facet.
The dinosaur lacks proximal pneumatopores in its dorsal ribs.
The proximal tibial condyle is narrow with its long axis oriented anteroposteriorly, and the upper surface of the tibia is narrow with its longitudinal axis directed from front to back.

Kaijutitan fossils were discovered in the Sierra Barrosa Formation near Rincón de los Sauces in Neuquén, Argentina, by researchers from two local museums. The skeleton of a large sauropod was discovered by technician Salvador Palomo in Cañadón Mistringa, Neuquén province, Argentina. Kaijutitan maui was named and described in 2019 by Leonardo Sebastián Filippi, Leonardo Salgado, and Carlos Alberto Garrido.

Kaijutitan is classified as a basal titanosaurian, outside the Eutitanosauria clade, alongside Epachthosaurus. It is one of the most basal titanosaurs characterized by procoelic tail vertebrae. Kaijutitan belongs to the parent group Lithostrotia and is classified within the class Saurischia.

Kaijutitan lived during the Late Cretaceous Coniacian stage, approximately 89 to 86 million years ago, in what is now South America. The remains were found in the upper Coniacian layer of the Sierra Barrosa Formation, dating to about 87 million years ago. The time range for Kaijutitan is estimated from 89.8 to 85.7 million years ago.
